title: Rotate and sanitize client dependencies; clean deprecated API surface
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce tech debt and improve platform stability by rotating pinned third-party dependencies across Python, JavaScript, and Go SDKs and removing legacy/deprecated API surface that creates maintenance burden.

Scope:
- Bump and test common networking and serialization libraries used by SDKs: Python (httpx, requests, pydantic), JS (node-fetch / undici, typescript types), Go (gohttp, protobuf, grpc).
- Remove deprecated API parameters and wrappers: specifically retire legacy 'response_wrapper' param, 'legacy_prompt_format' and the old streaming shim.
- Add explicit deprecation warnings in SDK runtime when deprecated fields are used.
- Run codemods to update common call sites in internal reference apps and examples.
- Publish migration guide and changelogs; coordinate canary rollout for hosted and dedicated customers.

Non-goals: full major-version redesign of SDK surface. Backwards-compatibility is preferred; breaking changes only where unavoidable and announced.

Acceptance criteria:
- All three language SDKs build and pass unit + integration suites on CI after dependency bumps.
- No new high/critical Snyk/OSS alerts introduced (or mitigations documented).
- Deprecated API fields emit runtime warnings and are documented in migration guide.
- Canary release (10% traffic) runs for 48h with error rate < baseline + 0.5% and latency regressions < 10%.
- Changelog and migration doc merged to docs repo and referenced in SDK release notes.

Migration notes for developers:
- Python: search for usages of 'response_wrapper' and replace with new 'output_format' and structured-output helpers. Example codemod: tools/codemods/py/replace_response_wrapper.py.
- JS: tests indicate undici 5.x provides ~6% latency improvement under high concurrency; bump and run jest/integration harness. Update types where 'PromptArgs' had deprecated fields.
- Go: replace old proto v1 types with v2 where necessary; run 'go vet' and regenerate clients with protoc v21.

Risks and mitigations:
- Breaking customers: add server-side compatibility layer that maps deprecated fields for one release cycle and logs usage. Notify top 10 customers directly.
- CI flakiness: add parallelization and retry in failing integration tests; hold rollouts behind canary gating.
- Security alerts on new deps: if a new bump introduces a vulnerability, pin to previous safe version and open a follow-on ticket to patch with patched release.

Artifacts and links:
- RFC / design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SDK+Dependency+Rotation+RFC
- Python PR (examples): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/987
- JS PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/1213
- Go PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/218
- Canary dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/canary/sdk-deps-rotation

Follow-ups:
- ENG-143215: publish client-2026.03 release notes and coordinate SDK blog post.
- ENG-143220: schedule post-release monitoring window and automated rollbacks if canary triggers fail.
